answer.answer: CD 109 Revision 1 says you need 5% superelevation for a 510 m radius curve at 100 kph on a rural road. For curves with radii less than those shown in Table 2.10 for "Minimum R with superelevation of 2.5%" (V2/R > 7), superelevation shall be provided in accordance with Equation 4.2 [CD 109 cl. 4.2]. Table 2.10 shows that at 100 kph the minimum R with superelevation of 2.5% is 1440 m and that 510 m is the "Desirable minimum R (superelevation 5%)" [CD 109 Table 2.10]. For rural areas, superelevation shall not exceed 7% except on existing roads or connector road loops [CD 109 cl. 4.3]. Decision support only; confirm against the current standard.

recordings.question: If a route has an AADT of 30,000, is it suitable for a WS2+1 road?

result.question: If a route has an AADT of 30,000, is it suitable for a WS2+1 road?

answer.answer: CD 109 Revision 1 says WS2+1 roads "should only be used for routes with a traffic flow of up to 25,000 vehicles annual average daily traffic (AADT)" [CD 109 cl. 6.1.1]. An AADT of 30,000 is above that advised upper level, so it is not suitable as a WS2+1 road unless the design team can justify a departure or alternative standard solution [CD 109 cl. 6.1.1]. This is a should-level criterion, so it is not an automatic Departure from Standard, but it does need recorded justification and engineer review [CD 109 cl. 6.1.1]. Decision support only; confirm against the current standard.

recordings.question: Would a 300 mm wide bollard be allowed in the stopping sight visibility envelope?

result.question: Would a 300 mm wide bollard be allowed in the stopping sight visibility envelope?

answer.answer: CD 109 Revision 1 says the stopping sight visibility envelope shall be free of obstructions by fixed objects, except for a fixed object with a width/length less than or equal to 550 mm [CD 109 cl. 3.4]. A 300 mm wide bollard is therefore allowed, because 300 mm is within that exception [CD 109 cl. 3.4]. This is a shall requirement [CD 109 cl. 3.4]. Decision support only; confirm against the current standard.

result.question: Would a 300 mm wide bollard be allowed in the stopping sight visibility envelope?

answer.answer: Yes, if the bollard is a single fixed object and its width is 300 mm, it is allowed in the stopping sight visibility envelope because CD 109 requires the envelope to be free of fixed-object obstructions except for a fixed object with a width/length less than or equal to 550 mm [CD 109 cl. 3.4]. A 300 mm bollard falls within that exception, so it does not need a Departure from Standard on width alone [CD 109 cl. 3.4]. If there is a group of bollards, their combined width/length must be 550 mm or less for the same exception to apply [CD 109 cl. 3.4]. Decision support only; confirm against the current standard.
